paper_metadata.title: Synthesis of a new tungsten-free c–c0 cobalt-based superalloy by tuning alloying additions

Alloy ingots of nominal compositions (in at.%) (1 /C0 x)Co–xNi–10Al–5Nb–2Nb (where x = 0, 10, 20, 30), weighing 30 g, were prepared by melting the constituent elements (four nine purity) under argon atmosphere using laboratory-scale vacuum arc melting unit with a water-cooled copper hearth and a tungsten electrode.
They were subsequently cast under an argon atmosphere into 3 mm rods and slabs using a vacuum arc casting unit equipped with a water-cooled copper mold.
Solutionizing of the cast rods was carried out at 1300 /C176C for 15 h under a vacuum of 10 /C06 mbar in a tube furnace, followed by quenching in cold water to obtain a supersaturated solid solution.
The sealed samples were peak aged at diﬀerent temperatures (generally 800 /C176C) in a box furnace and subsequently furnace cooled.

The microstructure reveals a ﬁne dendritic structure, with some solute segregation in the interdendritic regions (see S1).

Fig. 1b shows a typical microstructure from a sample quenched from the solutionizing temperature. The microstructure shows an equiaxed coarse-grained structure, with no dendritic segregation. The grain size for the solutionized alloy was determined to be around 150–400 microns.

The coherent precipitates have a cuboidal morphology that are distributed uniformly throughout the fcc c-Co matrix (Fig. 2a). These precipitates are within the size range of 30–60 nm and have a volume fraction of around 54% embedded in the c-Co matrix.

After heat treatment, these alloys exhibit a duplex microstructure with coherent cuboidal L1 2-ordered precipitates (c0) throughout the face-centred cubic matrix ( c), yielding a microstructure that is very similar to nickel-based superalloys as well as recently devel-oped Co–Al–W-based alloys.
